cards.text: The prophet Isaiah is passing along the LORD's own words, and they open like somebody shouting down a busy street. The LORD calls out, "Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters". And He's not done calling people in.

cards.question: The LORD also calls out to people who have no money at all. What does He tell them to do?
True or false: the wine and milk the LORD offers will cost them something.

cards.text: Then the LORD turns to what people have been spending their money and their hard work on.

cards.question: The LORD asks why people spend their money and their work on certain things. What's the trouble with those things?
Instead of chasing what doesn't satisfy, what does the LORD tell them to do?

cards.text: Listen and eat what is good, He says, and your soul will delight in the richest of foods. Then He says it again: lean in, come to Him, and listen, so your soul may live.

cards.question: The LORD promises to make a covenant with them. He says that covenant will last ___.

cards.text: An everlasting covenant, with the loving devotion He promised to David, Israel's king. Not a trial offer, friend. EVERLASTING.

cards.question: The LORD says He has made David a ___ to the nations, a leader and commander of the peoples.
The LORD goes on, "Surely you will summon a nation you do not know". What will nations who do not know you do?
True or false: the LORD says it's because He has bestowed glory on you.

cards.text: Now the message turns into a call to act while the door is open. "Seek the LORD while He may be found; call on Him while He is near."

cards.question: Next comes a call to forsake his way and his thoughts and return to the LORD. Who is it aimed at?
He's called to return to the LORD, that He may have compassion, and to our God, for He will ___ pardon.
Then the LORD speaks up about Himself. True or false: He says His thoughts are the same as our thoughts.
The LORD says His ways and thoughts are higher than ours. What does He compare that to?

cards.text: Now the LORD paints a picture from the weather: rain and snow falling from heaven.

cards.question: True or false: the rain and snow go back up without ever watering the earth.

cards.text: They water the earth so it buds and sprouts and gives seed to sow and food to eat. And the LORD says something of His works the same way.

cards.question: Just like the rain, the LORD says His ___ will not return to Him empty.
The LORD's word will accomplish what He pleases. What does He say it will do where He sends it?
The message closes with the people heading out. They will go out with ___ and be led forth in ___.

cards.text: The mountains and hills will burst into song before them, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands. Friend, I can't get ONE round of applause out of a cookie sheet.
Then the land itself changes. Instead of the thornbush, the cypress will grow, and instead of the brier, the myrtle will spring up.

cards.question: The LORD says all this will make a name for Him. What kind of sign will it be?

answers.text: A sign that fades in time

cards.text: And the LORD adds that this sign will never be destroyed. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer wondering if today was the day somebody tossed us all in the trash, so NEVER to be destroyed sounds real good to me.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin's voice is mostly missing. Only two story cards carry a real laugh: stop 1 card 9 and stop 2 cards 12 and 15. Several story cards are bare paraphrase with no personality, including stop 1 cards 4 and 7 and stop 2 cards 6 and 13. Stop 1 card 1's 'shouting down a busy street' is mild. Moments that could hold a laugh pass by with nothing, such as free wine and milk, spending money on what isn't bread, rain that never comes back without doing its job, and thornbushes swapped for cypress.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: 'An everlasting covenant...', 'Not a trial offer, friend.' and 'EVERLASTING.' Only the opening card can go past 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card opens by restating card 8's answer ('An everlasting covenant'), and its punchline ('EVERLASTING') repeats it again. Only the David detail moves the passage forward.

No story card sets up verse 4. The blank asks the baker to supply the exact word 'witness' from a line they haven't seen. The only way to reason it out is to rule out 'stranger' and 'threat', which don't fit 'leader and commander'. That tests wording, not the movement or meaning of the passage.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question says 'it's because He has bestowed glory on you.' The 'it' points back to card 11's answer, which is no longer on screen. The question never says what 'it' is: nations running to you.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question folds 'his way' and 'his thoughts' into one call aimed at one person. In Isaiah 55:7 the wicked man forsakes his way, and the unrighteous man forsakes his thoughts. The right answer, 'The wicked man', is only true for the way.

rule.text: A card about two groups needs an answer true for both. When a question covers more than one group, like the sea creatures and the birds, the right answer must be true for every group in it.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'He's called to return', which points back to the wicked man from card 2, and card 2 is no longer on screen. The capitalized 'He' also reads like God, the same pronoun used for the LORD later in the same sentence.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question turns the text's 'your thoughts' into 'our thoughts'. Card 5 does the same with 'higher than ours'. Isaiah 55:8-9 has the LORD speaking to 'you', so 'our' decides who is being spoken to and includes the baker and Papa Dorin.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'The LORD says something of His works the same way' calls it His 'works'. Isaiah 55:11 says 'My word'. Renaming it to hide card 9's answer misstates the text and can steer the baker away from 'word'.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
